title: Opening another application cancels launching animation of previous application
line: Launching a second app no longer removes the busy indicator from an app that is still starting.
explanation: KWin kept a single launch-feedback slot: every new activation token overwrote the previous one and destroyed its plasma activation object, which told the task manager the first launch had finished. On window activation it also only compared against the last token's app id. The change keeps a map from token to feedback, ends a token's feedback when its window activates with that token (or a window with the same app id appears or is activated), and leaves the other pending launches alone.

commits.message:
xdgactivation: keep launch feedback for every pending activation

Only the last requested token kept its launch feedback, so starting a
second app while the first was still loading removed the first app's
busy indicator. Track feedback per token and end only the window's own.

BUG: 492448

media.caption: Master: Slow Konsole clicked, then Slow Dolphin; from the second click on, Konsole loses its spinner and highlight (sweep tester's shots, ~1 s apart).
With the fix, same steps: both Slow Konsole and Slow Dolphin keep their spinners until their windows appear.
With the startup timeout raised to 30 s: both spinners end ~1.5 s after the Konsole and Dolphin windows appear, so KWin ends each feedback itself.

review.text: Tracking feedback per token is the right fix in the right place (KWin's single m_activation slot). But the old catch-all (any new active window cleared the feedback) is gone, so a launch whose window never arrives or has a different app id and no token keeps its PlasmaWindowActivationInterface and map entry forever, and startupRemoved is never sent for it. KWin maintainers will want this state bounded.
changes: Expire each pending activation after a timeout (e.g. the klaunchrc startup timeout or a fixed ~15-20 s) and emit startupRemoved / drop its feedback then, so m_activations cannot grow without bound.
